title: Payment Operations Standard — Missed Installments, Returned Installment Payments and Re-presentment under Payment Arrangements
content:
This standard covers, for Payment Arrangements, when an installment is recorded as missed, how a returned installment payment is booked, which returned debits are presented again, and when a missed installment is cured.

## 1. Recording an installment as missed

An installment is recorded as missed only when the handling date is later than the grace period counted from the installment's scheduled due date and the installment is not paid. Both facts are read from the plan's own records: the scheduled due date from the plan's schedule, and whether the installment is paid from the payments applied to it.

- While the handling date is on or before the last day of the grace period, the installment is not recorded as missed.
- From the day after that last day, an installment that is still not paid may be recorded as missed.
- An installment that is paid is not recorded as missed, whatever the date.

**Retired clause.** The clause under which the grace period was the type's manual grace in calendar days for a plan paid manually and the type's automatic-debit grace in calendar days for a plan collected by automatic debit, the day after the due date being day one, is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis. The type's grace figures themselves remain product figures of the type.

## 2. Returned installment payments

A returned installment payment is booked once against the payment it reverses. Whether a return has already been booked is read from the plan's installment history by the original payment it points to; a second return entry for the same original payment is not booked.

## 3. Re-presentment of returned debits

A returned ACH installment whose return reason is NSF (insufficient funds) is presented again after the type's re-presentment delay in business days, at most the type's number of ACH re-presentments per installment; returns for account closed, stop payment, unauthorized debit and card chargeback are never presented again. The re-presentments of an installment are counted as the ACH returns booked for that same installment.

| Return reason | Presented again |
|---|---|
| NSF on an ACH installment | Yes, after the type's delay, up to the type's maximum per installment |
| Account closed | Never |
| Stop payment | Never |
| Unauthorized debit | Never |
| Card chargeback | Never |

Hypothetical case: a debit-card installment charged back and an ACH installment returned for stop payment are both never presented again; an ACH installment returned for NSF is presented again after the type's delay, within the type's maximum.

## 4. Cure

A missed installment is cured when it is later paid in full.

superseded_clauses: The grace period is grace_period_days_manual calendar days for a plan paid manually and grace_period_days_autopay calendar days for a plan collected by automatic debit, the day after the due date being day one.
